:::{#sol-log-partition-normalization}

We start from the fact that the [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) integrates to one,
and isolate the factor $\expf{-\logpartitionf{\natparam}}$ that does not depend on $\rvar$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
1
&= \int \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(a density integrates to one)}\\
&= \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(@eq-exponential-family)}\\
&= \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, \expf{-\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the exponential of a sum is the product of the exponentials)}\\
&= \expf{-\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(a factor free of the integration variable moves out of the integral)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $\expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}
&= \expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, \expf{-\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(multiply both sides by } \expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam}} \text{)}\\
&= \expf{\logpartitionf{\natparam} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}} \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the product of exponentials is the exponential of the sum)}\\
&= \expf{0} \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(a number minus itself is zero)}\\
&= \int \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the exponential of zero is one)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
